v.1: An asker asked for a punishment sure to befall
v.2: —which none can avert from the faithless —
v.3: from Allah, Lord of the lofty stations.
v.4: The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a day whose span is fifty thousand years.
v.5: So be patient, with a patience that is graceful.
v.6: Indeed they see it to be far off,
v.7: and We see it to be near.
v.8: The day when the sky will be like molten copper,
v.9: and the mountains like [tufts of] dyed wool,
v.10: and no friend will inquire about [the welfare of his] friend,
v.11: [though] they will be placed within each other’s sight. The guilty one will wish he could ransom himself from the punishment of that day at the price of his children,
v.13: his kin, which had sheltered him
v.14: and all those who are upon the earth, if that might deliver him.
v.15: Never! Indeed, it is a blazing fire,
v.17: It invites him, who has turned back [from the truth] and forsaken [it],
v.19: Indeed man has been created covetous:
v.20: anxious when an ill befalls him
v.21: and grudging [charity] when good comes his way
v.23: those who persevere in their prayers
v.24: and there is a known share in whose wealth
v.25: for the beggar and the deprived,
v.26: and who affirm the Day of Retribution,
v.27: and those who are apprehensive of the punishment of their Lord
v.28: (there is indeed no security from the punishment of their Lord)
v.29: and those who guard their private parts
v.30: (apart from their spouses and their slave women, for then they are not blameworthy;
v.31: but whoever seeks beyond that—it is they who are the transgressors)
v.32: and those who keep their trusts and covenants,
v.33: and those who are observant of their testimonies,
v.34: and those who are watchful of their prayers.
v.35: They will be in gardens, held in honour.
v.36: What is the matter with the faithless that they scramble toward you,
v.37: from left and right, in groups?
v.38: Does each man among them hope to enter the garden of bliss?
v.39: Never! Indeed, We created them from what they know.
v.40: So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests that We are able
v.41: to replace them with [others] better than them and We are not to be outmaneuvered.
v.42: So leave them to gossip and play till they encounter the day they are promised:
v.43: the day when they emerge from graves, hastening, as if racing toward a target,
v.44: with a humbled look [in their eyes], overcast by abasement. That is the day they had been promised.
